recipes.name: Classic Caramel Corn
ingredients_raw: 0.5 cup Karo® Light OR Dark Corn Syrup
1 teaspoon Spice Islands® Pure Vanilla Extract

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 250 degrees F (120 degrees C). Spray a large shallow roasting pan with cooking spray, then fill with popped popcorn. Place in the preheated oven while preparing caramel.
Mix brown sugar, corn syrup, butter, and salt together in a heavy 2-quart saucepan over medium heat; stir constantly until mixture comes to a boil.
Stop stirring and boil mixture for 5 minutes.
Remove from heat and stir in vanilla and baking soda until well combined.
Pour caramel over warmed popcorn and stir until evenly coated.
Return to the oven and bake for 45 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Remove from the oven and spread onto a large aluminum foil sheet greased with cooking spray.
Cool, then break apart and store in a tightly covered container.

raw_recipe.headline: Classic Caramel Corn
raw_recipe.description: This easy caramel corn recipe makes a deliciously sweet and crunchy crowd-pleasing snack that’s great for get-togethers, picnics, and gifting.

With just a few simple ingredients and easy-to-follow steps, you can enjoy the perfect balance of crunchy, sweet caramel coating and fluffy popcorn goodness. Whether it's movie night or a special snack, this homemade caramel popcorn recipe will be your go-to for a mouthwatering sweet snack.

review.reviewBody: Do not make this caramel corn unless you plan to give it away, have rock solid will power, or the metabolism of a four year old. It is highly addictive. This past weekend I made it twice, once for a birthday gift and once because we were all sad to see it leave the house. I used dark corn syrup and followed the recipe exactly. To pop the popcorn, I put the kernels in a brown paper bag, folded the top over twice, and microwaved for 2-3 minutes. No oil needed. Repeat until you have 4 quarts. The only tip I'd suggest that isn't in the recipe already is to also spray the spoon or spatula you use to stir the corn with cooking spray. The pots and pans clean up easily after a soak in hot soapy water. Then you can relax and attempt to avoid eating the entire batch of caramel corn all at once.

Oh my, this was the best! I took the advice of others and sprayed a roasting pan, left the popcorn in the oven while the sauce was preparing. I also sprayed my spatula so nothing would stick. Drizzled it and stirred it. Helped to have someone mixing the popcorn around as I was drizzling it. Cooked it 45 min and stirred it every 10 min. Laid it out on parchment paper and it was delicious. Gone! Very easy, just time consuming because of the stirring but so easy for anyone to make and look like a pro! I am going to try adding peanuts and drizzle chocolate next time.

The only thing I changed was I put peanuts in it. I turned the oven up a little more around 300 and left it in another 15 minutes and the caramel was harder which I like the real crunchy not the mushy. Turned out very good!

If you are going to add peanuts , or any kind of nuts , i suggest that you add them to the caramel sauce before pouring onto the popcorn , otherwise they dont get covered and because they are heavier than popped corn , they do not stick and end up at the bottom of the bowl;

Delicious. I highly recommend baking in an enamel Dutch oven instead of on a pan. The Dutch oven holds plenty of heat, and gives you a nice vessel in which to stir the corn. I got much better coating and didn't spill anything, versus the pan which was challenging.

Turned out good. I did 1 hour @ 225 and stirred every 15. Turned out on bare marble island. 
For popping, put good 1/8th cup At a time in paper bag for 3 min in microwave.

I loved the recipe except I try to avoid corn syrup (Karo syrup) so I used 1/2 c Agave nectar in place of the Karo Syrup. Followed the rest of the recipe exactly but did spray my pan before I put the popcorn in it. It turned out FANTASTIC!!! My family loved it. You couldn’t even tell Karo syrup was not used. This recipe is a keeper (using Agave nectar of course).

I doubled the popcorn and tripled the caramel sauce.
Used pecans and butter ( no margarine)
Then lowered my oven temperature to 225 for 
45 minutes in middle of the.
No scorching and wonderful flavor

I love this recipe it is the same or close to the one I made as a teen all the time, only back then we didn't bake it. I like the baked better. My change is I bake at 300 degrees. This makes the carmel melt more and easier to stir. I do four 10 minute stirs then stir while cooling till cool and crunchy then I store in Tupperware and it last fors days or until it is all ate as I make a double or triple batch.

I have made this recipe several times sometimes I put salted peanuts in it. I pop my own kernels with my air popper. 1/2 kernels makes the perfect amount of popped popcorn. This is my go to recipe and I will not use another caramel corn recipe. I have attempted many before finding this one. I use parchment paper instead of spraying a baking dish.
This turned out fabulous!! I added cocktail peanuts and lined cookie sheets with parchment paper. 4 of us ate the entire batch!! MAGNIFICENT

I used a 3 qt. baking dish to make 2 qts. of popcorn, but it was a bit too small to work easily in. There was enough room just for baking, but in stirring there's too little wiggle room to keep the popcorn inside easily, so use a bigger dish or 2 pans. This was fast and easy to put together, but even so my caramel sauce looked fluffy and foamy and not at all like the picture in the directions. The color was the same, but the texture of mine wasn't smooth like that, it appeared with so many more air bubbles in it and was fluffy. It didn't mix too well with the popcorn. I think the heat may be too low to keep the sugar melted enough for mixing. I've made caramel corn several times before using other recipes and the caramel has always mixed in given enough time and patience. This one is difficult and I am not having the same success I am used to. I don't know if it's the recipe, the weather outside, the oven temp, me, or any combination thereof that is the issue. The flavor on this is great and it did turn out crispy on the pieces that had caramel on them, but sadly, too many of them barely had any caramel. It seemed like there was enough sauce, just that it never got hot enough again to melt to a stirrable texture so it clumped to the popcorn in clusters and didn't really coat any of the pieces entirely. That's my theory anyway. 45 minutes in the oven and it still didn't look much different as far as distribution then when it started.

My husband says “This is fire!” Excellent recipe, followed recipe other than adding pecans and peanuts to the caramel before pouring on popcorn. I stir every 15 minutes and then pour on parchment paper to cool.

I loved it! I added salted cashews and unsalted pecans to it. YEP...it was scrumptious! Follow directions exactly. Although the recipe doesn't specify light or dark brown sugar, I used light cuz that's all I had. It is definitely addictive.
Easy to make and everytime we served it or give it as a treat gift, people love it.
So butter and crunchy. Everyone loves it. I can't make enough!

I love making Carmel corn when the grandkids come over. This is the first recipe I've tried that did not involve a candy thermometer. It made it so easy. Both my wife and I agree this is without a doubt the very best I've ever made. I am wondering if it's because it wasn't heated so high. Either way, this will be my go to recipe from now on

I make this with puffed corn, Its delicious and is easier to eat with dental work no shells tastes the same. I use a large bag and double the recipe of carmel. wow to say its additive doesnt seem to be enough. Getting it bagged up to put in christmas gifts.

I have made this recipe for decades and it has been delicious! this morning I made a batch. The caramel is grainy like the sugar didn't melt. I followed the recipe like I always do. What causes this issue? I don't want to make another batch until I know what I did wrong.
Just what I was craving! Will make again adding nuts and maybe a chocolate drizzle.
